title: Button to show Virtual Keyboard in KScreenLocker does not work unless the user manually enables Plasma Keyboard in the virtual keyboard setting
line: The lock screen's Show On-Screen Keyboard button now opens Plasma Keyboard even when no virtual keyboard is enabled in System Settings.
explanation: The lock screen button calls KWin's forceActivate(), which since the fix for bug 467209 shows the keyboard even when it is set to never show, but only if an input method process is running. With the default settings (no virtual keyboard chosen in System Settings) KWin starts none, so the button had nothing to show. The login manager avoids this by starting KWin with --inputmethod plasma-keyboard; the lock screen had no equivalent. Now forceActivate() while the screen is locked and with no input method configured starts Plasma Keyboard (from its desktop file), and KWin stops it again on unlock, so the user's setting is unchanged afterwards.

commits.message:
inputmethod: start Plasma Keyboard for the lock screen when none is set

The lock screen's on-screen keyboard button did nothing unless an input
method was configured in the settings. When it asks for the keyboard
while locked, now start Plasma Keyboard and stop it again on unlock.

BUG: 527077

media.caption: Default settings, locked, after clicking Show On-Screen Keyboard: nothing appears
Same click with the fix: Plasma Keyboard opens on the lock screen

review.text: Fixing this in KWin's InputMethod is the right layer since KWin owns the input method process lifecycle. Launching org.kde.plasma.keyboard.desktop on demand from forceActivate() only when locked and no input method is configured, and stopping it again on KSldApp::unlocked via m_lockScreenInputMethod, restores the lock screen OSK button without altering the user's configured virtual keyboard or affecting unlocked sessions. The patch is minimal, properly guarded by KWIN_BUILD_SCREENLOCKER, and backed by passing KWin autotests and clear before/after screenshots.
